messages:
Alex: heads-up — escalated Intercom ticket from customer acct_83B claiming promo credits were consumed before their free-tier monthly credits. They say the promo was non-expiring but dashboard shows promo spent and free credits left.

Maria: thanks Alex. ticket id? can you paste the customer's message? also which invoice they saw this on?

Alex: ticket #IC-45218 pasted below.

Alex: "Customer: We were charged against promo credits on 2026-03-12 even though our free monthly credits should be used first. Balance shows 0 promo, 120 free left. Invoice inv_20260312_009 shows promo line item applied. Please advise."

Sam: assigning to billing eng. initial hypothesis: promo with precedence flag got set to HIGH in the ledger when the promo was created. this can force promo to be used first. i'll check promo config.

Sam: quick repro steps i'm running: 1) create test acct with free_tier 200, 2) apply promo code PROMO-UX20 with priority=high and expiry=null, 3) simulate usage 300 tokens across two calls, 4) run charge simulation. i can share DB query.

Sam: query i ran:
```
SELECT credit_type, available, used, priority FROM billing_credits WHERE account_id='acct_test_123';
-- result: promo, 0, 200, priority=10; free_tier, 100, 100, priority=1
```

Sam: result shows promo token bucket with higher priority consumed first. looks like priority column used in charge algorithm.

Ryan: that's a bug if promotions without expiry default to higher precedence. charging code should prefer buckets by expiry ascending then priority descending is wrong. expected behavior: prefer free_tier first (internal policy) unless promo explicitly marked "use-first".

Maria: customer insists promo was not marked use-first. the promo metadata: promo_id=promo_202511_acq, created by marketing. Sam can you fetch promo metadata? also send a customer-facing explanation and ETA.

Sam: fetched metadata: name="UX Onboarding 20", created_by=marketing@redwood.com, start_date=2025-11-12, expiry=null, attributes=["non-expiring", "marketing-acq"], precedence=null, notes="created via promo ui bulk upload"

Sam: interesting — precedence is NULL in promo table but billing_credits entry shows priority=10. looks like the migration that sets default priority for legacy promos set HIGH for NULLs. paging @Jenna for migrations knowledge.

Jenna: I ran that migration last year to normalize priorities. the script defaulted NULL->10 to avoid NPEs in older runtime. i can roll a hotfix to set default to 0 for free-tier-like promos but we need to decide safe scope.

Jenna: proposed fix: 1) backfill billing_credits for active promos where promo.attributes contains "marketing-acq" and precedence IS NULL -> set priority=0, 2) update charge algorithm to treat free_tier bucket as precedence -1, 3) add unit test. i can push a patch to billing-service canary tonight.

Sam: sounds good. can we also add a customer-visible audit event showing which bucket was charged per request so we don't have to manually inspect DB for future escalations?

Ryan: yes that's low-risk and helpful. add to backlog but maybe don't block the hotfix.

Maria: ETA for canary deploy? customer expects update within 48h.

Jenna: I can deploy canary within 6h if we cut a small CL. will run charge-sim tests across sample of accounts.

Sam: customer-facing message draft: 
"Hi! Thanks for the report — we've identified that older promos created before a priority field existed were assigned a high default priority during a past migration, which caused them to be consumed before monthly free credits. We are preparing a hotfix to update affected promo buckets and to change the charging logic so monthly free credits are preferred. We'll canary the fix within ~6 hours and follow up once completed. We will also refund any inadvertent promo consumption. Apologies for the confusion."

Maria: looks good. send it and CC billing-sre. also create internal incident so we can track refunds and affected accounts.

BillingBot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-12-BILLPROMO. Affected_accounts_count: 12.

Alex: customer replied: "Thanks, please expedite. A few of our customers rely on these credits for demos this week."

Sam: running a script to list affected accounts now. sample output:
```
acct_83B: promo_used=200, free_remaining=120, invoice=inv_20260312_009
acct_92F: promo_used=50, free_remaining=450, invoice=inv_20260228_004
acct_701: promo_used=200, free_remaining=0, invoice=inv_20260301_012
... total 12 accounts
```

Jenna: canary started. deploying patch to billing-service v1.12.3-canary. running e2e charge-sim against 100 test accounts.

Jenna: canary results: pass. no regression on expiry-handling. rolling patch to prod cutoff window in 30m.

Maria: pls confirm refund workflow. finance and customer success need amounts and invoice refs.

Sam: creating refund SQL to credit back promo tokens and add invoice adjustments. example:
```
UPDATE billing_credits SET available=available+used, used=0 WHERE account_id='acct_83B' AND credit_type='promo';
INSERT INTO invoice_adjustments (invoice_id, amount, reason) VALUES ('inv_20260312_009', -12.00, 'promo erroneously consumed before free-tier credits');
```

Sam: will coordinate with finance on GL codes. setting follow-up in incident.

Alex: customer updated: "Appreciate the quick response. Please confirm when refund is applied."

Maria: refund ETA? Jenna, will the backfill touch live accounts immediately?

Jenna: backfill job will run after deploy and will update affected billing_credits rows. it will run in small batches with idempotency checks; expected to complete in ~45m for 12 accounts. refunds will be queued to finance for approval; once finance posts them they'll appear on customer invoices as credit memos.

Maria: thanks team. I'll update the customer with expected refund timeframe and CC finance.

Alex: closing loop: customer reply: "Refund shows on our invoice as credit memo. thanks for the help."
